correctness.rationale: The finite simple graph is exactly the categorical product C_7×K_4 on 28 vertices, adjacent for cyclic displacement ±1 and unequal colours. Independently reconstructed all 36,068 nonempty independent faces and the lexicographic vertex-toggle matching (18,023 disjoint pairs); topologically sorted the entire reversed-matched oriented Hasse digraph with 218,008 incidences and all 36,068 faces, proving acyclicity. There is exactly one critical 0-cell, nine critical 3-cells and twelve critical 4-cells. Independent signed gradient-path elimination reproduces each of the 108 entries of the pinned 9×12 Morse boundary; a separate sympy ZZ Smith normal form yields six unit factors and three zero diagonal factors. An independently constructed full simplicial mod-2 reduction gives b_0=1,b_3=3,b_4=6 with all other Betti numbers zero. The discrete Morse CW complex has no 1- or 2-cells; the Hurewicz identification π_3(∨^9 S^3)≅Z^9 identifies attaching maps of its twelve 4-cells with the integer matrix. Unimodular basis transformations are realized by wedge self-equivalences; six unit cones cancel and leave ∨^3S^3∨∨^6S^4. Finite exhaustive calculation is an exact finite proof, not an all-parameter assertion. The mod-2 computation alone does not prove integral torsion-freeness.

originality.rationale: The primary 2023 paper specifically names C_7×K_4 but proves only support in consecutive homology dimensions and an allowed Moore-space wedge type; it asks whether integral torsion always vanishes. Its free-homology observations are explicitly credited. The present full integer Morse differential with six unit Smith factors rules out those Moore components and yields an exact integral homotopy type; this conclusion is not implied by that theorem or by inspected complete×complete, path-factor, or generalized-Mycielskian results. Resultary searches found the exact claim only as the present record; searches do not establish absolute novelty, and unpublished Sage data are a concrete priority risk.
residual_risks: Possible unindexed equivalence or unpublished Sage/auxiliary computation by the 2023 authors for this explicitly named graph; original paper records that free homology in both degrees was already observed, and no private logs or new releases were inspected.

The finite invariant was not a routine consequence of the prior theorem: it requires a substantive 36,068-face acyclic discrete-Morse certificate and signed integer Smith calculation. Its scope remains one natural finite instance, not a complete solution to the general torsion question.
